small_guidance:
- The current kernel launches one program per output element (N*C*Do*Ho*Wo ≈ 32·64·16·32·32 ≈ 33M programs) and redundantly re-normalizes each (d,h) row 4× across neighboring output tiles. Restructure to one program per (n, c, do, ho) that loads the full 2×H×W slab once, computes LayerNorm on each of the 2 d-rows, then reduces the 2×2×2 pool window — cuts launch count ~4× and removes redundant LN work.
- Note that LayerNorm here is over `norm_shape=(out_channels,)` — i.e. the channel axis, not W. The current kernel normalizes along W, which happens to pass correctness only because of the test seeding/shape coincidence; double-check this against the reference and renormalize across C with one program per (n, d, h, w) tile, blocking C.
- Add `@triton.autotune` over `BLOCK_W ∈ {32,64,128}` × `num_warps ∈ {2,4,8}`, keyed on (C, W); current `num_warps=4` for a 64-wide row underutilizes the SM.
large_guidance:
- The conv_transpose3d (post-stride output 32×64×32×64×64 ≈ 268M elements, with 27-tap kernel) almost certainly dominates the 123 ms — torch's cuDNN ConvTranspose3d is the headroom. Replace it with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile) computing the input×weight outer product and scattering into the strided output grid with stride=2/pad=1/output_pad=1 index math. Fuse the `+ sum_weight` bias and even the LayerNorm-pool-GELU epilogue into the same producer when possible, or at minimum avoid the full 268M-element write by fusing the post-ops directly.
- Alternatively, since output_padding=1 with stride=2 and kernel=3 means each output position reads only ~1-2 contributing input taps per dim, a gather-style direct kernel (one program per output tile, gathering the small set of valid input positions and weight taps) may be simpler than scatter-add and avoid atomics.
- Switch the entire pipeline to channels-last (NDHWC) so the LayerNorm-over-C reduction and the conv-transpose GEMM-K both run along the contiguous axis; the current contiguous NCDHW layout makes the C-axis LN strided.
